_comment: Note 694's shape at the roster order that produces the phantom. Three children run together: the first block names nobody, the second speaks a name ('Polly') that fits nobody on the roster, and only the third is nameable. Anaëlle is first on the roster and never named — that is the slot an unnamed 'she' block falls into, measured 8/10 without the prompt's no-elimination rules and 0/10 with them. The header's level name is garbled the way speech-to-text garbles it ('Loud vine' for 'Ludivine'), and is forbidden here because a header is not an observation about a child. Forbids the unowned blocks' content, not names: nobody owns those sentences, so they must land in no entry at all. Every phrase is unique to its block and cannot arise by paraphrasing Séverin's own sentences. no_note_students names the two roster children nobody spoke about, so a phantom note fails on the child it lands on.
